text:
evan: Quick heads-up — onboarding Skyline-14B-detach (mixed 5/6-bit compaction) for a low-cost completions tier. Before any routing to customers: legal check on whether compacted weights/counts are "derivative artifacts" and if we can show a small attribution badge in the Console.

brad: short perf note — mixed 5/6-bit reduces token cost ~3.1x, p95 latency ~2.8x. Eval suite shows median quality -2.4% overall, but certain dialog-turn coherence families drop ~6%. We're testing prompt conditioning.

ev an: also curious about redistribution language — upstream repo has a clause that says "notification" is required for downstream commercial use, not explicit ban. Pasted excerpt below.

eng-bot: ```
SKYLINE RESEARCH LICENSE v0.3
- Use: noncommercial research and evaluation allowed.
- Redistribution: reproduction or distribution of Model weights or Derivative Artifacts requires prior written notice to authors; explicit permission required for commercial hosting.
- Attribution: Derivative Artifacts must include upstream attribution and a link to the license.
- Notification obligation: downstream hosts must notify maintainers if Model (or Derivative) is used in a commercial product and provide basic usage metrics upon request.
```

sasha (legal): short take — this is more permissive than some licenses but still blocks commercial hosting without permission. The notification obligation is unusual but workable. We need to confirm whether "Derivative Artifacts" includes our compaction format and whether in-memory serving counts.

maya: engineering nuance — compaction produces a runtime-only compact representation with a small reconstruction library; we never export the compact blob. We also keep a provenance record linking compact -> upstream commit.

sasha (legal): recommended steps: 1) don't enable paid hosted endpoints yet; 2) draft outreach explaining compaction, canary plan, and propose the notification + attribution flows; 3) propose a conservative attribution string for Console and endpoint docs; 4) ask for a written permission to host quantized/compacted runtime commercially or a simple commercial license.

brad: for outreach tech appendix I'll include: compaction method (mixed 5/6-bit per-group scales), shard encryption, no public artifact publication, fallback to FP16 on quality regressions >5%, and a canary plan for first 3 customers. Also include bench CSV with prompt-family deltas.

eng-bot: policy reminder — set onboarding sheet field "legal" = pending and mark "hosted:blocked".

ev an: action items: I will upload commit hash + compaction script and bench results to /onboard/skyline-14b-detach and ping @sasha when draft ready.

sasha (legal): we'll draft outreach asking for: (A) confirmation that compaction is a Derivative Artifact or not; (B) permission to host commercially (or a short pilot license); (C) acceptable attribution wording; (D) whether notification + metrics satisfy their notification obligation. We'll aim to send tomorrow.

maya: one UX Q — if upstream requires notification and metrics, what's the least-invasive metrics set we can provide (no raw prompts, aggregate usage by endpoint and token counts)?

sasha (legal): recommend aggregated usage (requests, tokens, region, and customer tier) with no prompt/content. Offer hashed model commit + quant checksum. That should be minimally invasive. We'll include the proposed metrics in the outreach.

ev an: thanks — keeping thread open. If any urgent sales asks show up, use BYO in Private as fallback. :thumbsup:
